heading: INT. GRAND OPERA HOUSE - STAGE - REHEARSAL DAY

units.text: INT. GRAND OPERA HOUSE - STAGE - REHEARSAL DAY
An empty stage in work light.
Painted flats of a Venetian canal lean against the wall.
A grand piano sits center stage, its lid propped.
High above, a chandelier is wrapped in plastic like a pinata.
ILARIA BONACCORSI, 40s, the pianist, plays a slow arpeggio.
At the lip of the stage, a conductor, GASTON FEUERSTEIN, 60s, taps his baton on the music stand.
In the wings, a stagehand, NKEM OKONJO-DREW, 30s, adjusts a rope.
In the pit, a violinist, BRYNMOR LLOYD-PRICE, 20s, tunes, and a soprano, ADELHEID MARQUARDT, 30s, in a rehearsal robe, hums to herself in a corner.
Nobody speaks.
The arpeggio rolls.
Gaston raises an eyebrow, and Ilaria stops, and the silence fills the hall.
Brynmor slips out of the pit and into the wings, and Nkem passes him a coil of rope without looking.
Above them the chandelier creaks.
Everyone looks up.
The chain is slipping.
A link clicks.
Adelheid steps back from her corner.
Nkem drops the rope.
Ilaria slams the piano lid shut and Gaston dives for the music stand, and all five scramble toward the wings as the chandelier lurches, swings, and hangs, quivering, by a single thread of steel.
For a moment nobody breathes.
Then Adelheid begins to laugh.
